MATH ENGINE ~194 EXPERIMENTS 6 OPERATIONS · 6 INVARIANTS

RGI Mathematics

A small set of typed objects, a fixed set of pure operations, six invariants that hold by construction, and a certification discipline. Together, they make self-improvement auditable, approvable, and safe.

Source: Cross-Graph Attention: A Governed Math Engine That Reshapes Decisions From Verified Outcomes — Arindam Banerji, PhD

Controlled experiments · synthetic + production-structure data · no production customers

Key Terms (expand)

μ — centroid prototypes (learned positions in factor space)

σ — per-factor outcome-conditioned variance (diagnostic only)

DK — DiagonalKernel (per-factor distance weights; L2 identity = default)

R — append-only hash-chained verified outcome record

K — routing memory (which evidence proved decisive)

α — category coverage over a sliding window

q — observed accuracy on verified outcomes

V — verified volume (total verified decisions)

θ_min — conservation floor derived from deployment tensor shape

η — learning rate (η_confirm = 0.05, η_override = 0.01)

τ — temperature for softmax confidence (default 0.1)

γ — re-convergence ratio (post-shock speed / initial speed)

ε_firm — firm-specific deviation from population centroid

IKS — Institutional Knowledge Score (composite health metric)

GAE — Graph Attention Engine (the compute layer)

LVQ — Learning Vector Quantization (centroid update family)

TPF — Tech-Process Fusion (target surface improvement)

SA — Situation Analyzer (regime-aware routing)

AE — AgentEvolver (runtime strategy evolution)

RGI improves every decision, the system that makes it, and the systems it targets. RSI improves the model.
This page is the math that makes it work — the typed objects, pure operations, structural invariants, and experiment evidence. Not a tutorial. Not a pitch. The specification.

The Abstraction

Every number the engine emits carries a complete chain of custody:

object read → operation applied → invariant that protected it → tier that certifies it

  • Graph engineering reads a graph to retrieve answers and routes a graph of agents to dispatch work
  • RGI reshapes the graph from verified outcomes — a third operation the other two cannot produce
  • The engine is a hardened math engine: objects, operations, invariants, certification
  • The decision rule (argmin distance) is written by no operation — self-improvement and a fixed decision procedure coexist by construction

What this is NOT

  • Not unconstrained online learning — centroids update only from verified human outcomes, behind a three-layer conservation gate. No regret bound — conservation replaces it.
  • Not contextual bandits — no arm pull, no exploration-exploitation tradeoff. The conservation gate decides when to learn, not a bandit policy.
  • Not RLHF — no reward model, no preference ranking. The correctness signal is a verified outcome, not a human preference.
  • Not a GNN — no message passing, no graph neural network. Cross-graph attention is scaled dot-product attention across heterogeneous schemas.
  • The engine is the statics — objects, operations, invariants. The loops that sequence them over time are the architecture (§10 of the paper). The test: a noun on state is the engine; a verb that sequences operations is the architecture.

Layer 1 — State: What the Engine Knows

Setting
  • A domain expert faces a stream of decisions, each described by a factor vector v ∈ [0,1]d
  • Each decision belongs to one of nc categories and has na possible actions
  • After acting, the expert (not the system) verifies the outcome: confirm or override
  • Goal: recommend actions that improve over time from verified outcomes, under a conservation constraint that prevents learning from insufficient or corrupted evidence
  • Sized by one triple: nc categories × na actions × d factors
  • SOC: 6×4×6 = 144 prototypes. S2P: 5×5×7 = 175. Trading: 5×3×6 = 90.
  • Small enough that every object is auditable, every operation is cheap
  • A few hundred verified outcomes move the geometry
ObjectLifecycleMeaningWho writes
μevolvingPrototypes of a good decision per (category, action)update rule only
KevolvingWhich evidence proved decisive, per categoryupdate rule only
σevolvingPer-factor outcome-conditioned variance (diagnostic)diagnostic only
Rappend-onlyHash-chained verified outcomes — certifies everythingverification only
GrefreshedEvidence substrate (four clocks)ingestion
DKconfiguredPer-factor weights (L2 identity = default)calibration only
a*( · )FIXEDargmin over μ under DK — the decision formNOBODY
  • a* has no write lane — the functional form (argmin distance under DK) is fixed. Centroids μ move — that's learning. The decision procedure that reads them never changes. This is the invariant that makes self-improvement approvable.
  • σ is diagnostic, not a scoring weight — it surfaces the trust trap but is walled off from DK (I2)

Layer 2 — Operations: Six Pure Transforms

Each operation is a function with a signature and a contract. The loop supplies timing; the operation is the same function called once or ten-thousand times.

Decision scoring flow

The code — ~844 parameters, no LLM, O(1) per decision

# The entire scoring + learning engine
class CompoundingScorer:
    """Score → verify → reshape centroids.
    ~844 parameters. No LLM. No GPU. O(1) per decision."""

    def score(self, factors, category) -> ScoreResult:
        v = np.array(factors)
        μ = self._graph_store.get_centroids(category)
        d_sq = {a: np.sum((v - μ[a]) ** 2) for a in self._actions}
        logits = {a: -d_sq[a] / self._tau for a in self._actions}
        probs = softmax(logits)
        best = max(probs, key=probs.get)
        return ScoreResult(action=best, confidence=probs[best])

    def learn(self, factors, action_index, category, confirmed):
        """LVQ centroid update — conservation-gated."""
        η = 0.05 if confirmed else 0.01
        v = np.array(factors)
        μ_old = centroids[category][action_index]
        μ_new = μ_old + η * (v - μ_old)  # LVQ: μ ← μ + η(v - μ)
        gate = self._conservation_gate.check(centroids, μ_new, category)
        if not gate.passed:
            return LearnResult(accepted=False, reason=gate.reason)
        self._graph_store.save_centroids(centroids)
        return LearnResult(accepted=True, displacement=gate.displacement)
# The three-layer conservation gate
class ConservationGate:
    """Three layers, all fixed at deployment approval.
    Learning cannot alter them. The gate protects the geometry."""

    def check(self, old_centroids, new_centroids, category):
        α = self._current_phase()          # category coverage
        V = self.tensor_volume              # verified decisions
        disp = np.linalg.norm(new - old)    # centroid displacement
        max_disp = 23.53 / (α * V)          # θ_min
        if disp > max_disp:
            return GateResult(passed=False, reason="exceeds_threshold")
        # Layer 2: no single factor drifts > 0.7× total displacement
        for j in range(len(new)):
            if abs(new[j] - old[j]) > 0.7 * disp:
                return GateResult(passed=False, reason="factor_drift")
        return GateResult(passed=True, displacement=disp)

The six operations in detail

score(v, Θ) → (a, p, m)

Contrast with other architectures:

  • RLHF: the reward model's weights are the decision rule — and they change during training. Here, a* is fixed by construction.
  • Neural scoring: millions of parameters, none individually auditable. Here, ~844 parameters — the sum of all copilots' centroid prototypes (nc×na×d each: SOC 144 + S2P 175 + Trading 90 + Purchasing 120 + DataOps 180 = 709), plus K routing memory, DK kernel, and configured constants. A regulator can inspect every centroid.
  • LLM-as-judge: the decision rule changes with every model update. Here, you can switch the LLM and the judgment geometry is untouched.
  • Action = distance to nearest centroid, not a reward maximization
  • Confidence = calibrated softmax, not raw probability
  • Margin = gap between top two actions (how decisive)
  • Reads μ, DK, τ. Writes nothing.

update(Θ, v, y) → Θ'

  • The one operation that reshapes the geometry
  • Asymmetric learning rates: confirm 5×, override 1× (penalty ratio ρ)
  • Fires only on verified human outcomes, never the system's own guess (I5)

route(v, Θ) → k*

  • Three signals composed: precision + leverage + discriminative
  • No separately trained acquisition model — derived from the same geometry

gate(R, θ_min, ...) → {GREEN, AMBER, RED}

  • Three-layer test — any layer can pause the system
  • Reads R and constants. Writes nothing. Cannot be optimized around (I4).

attend(G_i, G_j) → discovery

  • softmax(Ei EjT/√d)·Vj — scaled dot-product attention across heterogeneous graph embeddings
  • Operates on learned embeddings (unbounded), not on bounded [0,1] factor vectors — this is why dot product works here but L2 wins in score()
  • route's operator applied between graph domains rather than within one
  • Same mathematical object, different role — one operator family spans scoring, acquisition, and discovery

separate(Θ) → σ

  • Per-factor outcome-conditioned variance from R
  • Surfaces the trust trap — the factor analysts trust most that is actually noisiest
  • Walled off from DK by I2 (σ⊥μ separation)

Layer 3 — Invariants: What Holds by Construction

These hold as a matter of the mathematics, not of careful operation. They are why the engine is hardened.

I1
Decision-form invariance
The functional form a* = argmin‖v−μ‖²_DK is fixed — no operation alters it. Centroids μ move (that's learning); the decision procedure that reads them never changes. Self-improvement and a fixed decision rule coexist by construction.
I2
σ⊥μ separation
E[Δμ] = η·(GT − μ) is σ-independent. Learning (moves μ) and enrichment (reduces σ) are independent to first order (~1% coupling). A better data feed lifts day-one accuracy but does not change how fast the system learns.
I3
A0: acquisition, not depth
With graph frozen and enrichment inert, iterating over unchanged evidence cannot improve the decision. Depth is acquisition, never loop count.
I4
Conservation is exogenous
gate reads R and deployment constants (θ_min, window size, baseline ratios) — never the current decision, never any parameter the loop optimizes. The conservation thresholds are fixed at deployment approval. The loop cannot optimize around the gate.
I5
Append-only certified record
R is hash-chained and append-only. Update fires only on human-verified outcomes, never on the system's own guess. Integrity failure forces RED.
I6
Re-convergence
After a shock the system re-converges faster than it first converged: γ > 1 ⟺ ε_firm > 0.125. Institutional memory is an asset against change.
  • I5 supplies certified signal
  • I1 confines where it writes
  • I4 governs when it acts
  • I2 keeps the two learning engines separable
  • I3 bounds what iteration claims
  • I6 makes accumulated geometry pay off after a shock
  • Remove any one → a specific failure opens (5 confirmed + I4 boundary defined at 50–60% adversarial intensity — table below)

Invariant ablation — what breaks when you remove each one

Systematic ablation: each invariant removed individually, 2000 decisions × 5 seeds, bootstrap 95% CIs. Full engine untouched.

InvariantFullAblatedDelta [95% CI]Failure observedStatus

I1 Decision form70.6%61.4%+9.19 pp [8.29, 10.12]661–738 decision-form switches per seed — instabilityCONFIRMED
I5 Certified record68.6%62.0%+6.67 pp [5.72, 7.55]667 uncertified self-training updates — noise amplificationCONFIRMED
I3 Acquisition, not depth70.6%66.8%+3.75 pp [2.94, 4.62]1.2–1.9% action flips on unchanged evidence probesCONFIRMED

  • I6 produced the largest failure — random reset after shock lost 12.08pp. Accumulated geometry IS the asset.
  • I1 instability is dramatic — hundreds of decision-form switches per seed. Fixed a* is not a theoretical nicety.
  • I4 has a sharp protection boundary at 50–60% adversarial intensity. Below 50%: the other invariants absorb the damage and the engine self-corrects. Above 60%: I4 prevents +8pp to +34pp accuracy loss. The transition is sharp, not gradual. Penalty ratios and pairwise interactions are secondary — intensity is the dominant axis.

Six reasons the math is load-bearing

① Without Situation Analyzer → no truly autonomous agents
  • Agentic frameworks dispatch with heuristic routers — they decode, they don't reason about the situation
  • Day-one accuracy: SA 78.2% vs fixed-baseline 72.3% (+5.9pp, p<0.0001)
  • ~844 parameters. No LLM. No GPU.
② Without TPF → process changes are manual art
  • Process mining shows WHERE. Cannot tell you WHY, fix it, or transfer the fix.
  • With TPF: −63% exceptions on the same bottleneck
  • Without reification, every bottleneck is a fresh 4–6 hour investigation
③ Without AgentEvolver → frozen production systems
  • Can't change the engine on a flying airplane — unless it's conservation-gated
  • 7 variants tested, 1 promoted, 6 rejected (conservation, correctness floor, variance)
  • Evolves AI systems AND the targets of AI systems
④ Graph math → judgment geometry matters
  • Knowledge graphs store facts. No graph system brings judgment geometry.
  • L2 97.9% vs dot product 60.9% — +36.99pp (5 kernels tested; L2 ties Mahalanobis, beats all others)
  • L2 preserves boundary sensitivity that cosine erases
⑤ Conservation → knows where it stops working
  • 9,826 checks across 5 copilots. <5% false-pause rate.
  • Sustained degradation: 100%. Drift: 100%. Sudden regime break: 100%.
  • Sparse targeted poisoning: boundary named at 57% — a strength, not a gap
⑥ Without enrichment → every decision starts with same context
  • RSI improves weights. RGI enriches context — and it compounds.
  • The 1,000th investigation traverses a richer graph than the 1st
  • This is data intelligence: data that learns about itself

What This Architecture Delivers

The state, operations, and invariants above compose into a system with properties no other architecture in the literature provides.

What the math gives you
  • Self-improvement without weight updates — the model is frozen; the decision infrastructure compounds from verified outcomes. No fine-tuning, no RLHF, no retraining.
  • A decision rule whose functional form no operation can alter — a* = argmin distance under DK. Centroids move (learning); the procedure that reads them is fixed. The invariant that makes self-improvement approvable.
  • Independent learning and enrichment — σ⊥μ separation (I2). Buying a better data feed and learning from decisions are independent investments. Proven, ~1% coupling.
  • A conservation law the loop cannot game — gate reads R, not the current decision or any optimizable parameter (I4). This is structural, not a threshold someone tuned.
  • Recovery that accelerates — γ > 1. Accumulated geometry is an asset after a shock. Proved four ways, confirmed in simulation.
What no other architecture provides
  • A fourth cognitive-architecture memory type — beyond episodic, semantic, and procedural. Judgment memory (outcome-conditioned quality decompositions) cannot be derived from read or route. Only reshape produces it.
  • The trust trap — the factor your team trusts most has the highest outcome-conditioned variance. No dashboard, no episodic memory, no semantic memory can surface this. Only reshape can.
  • Cross-domain discovery that scales as n^{2.11} — the same operator that scores within a domain discovers between domains. One operator family, two roles.
  • A compounding exponent > 1 — cumulative advantage is super-linear (1.387, CI excludes 1). The system accelerates. Measured, not modeled.
  • Published boundaries — ~66 foundational + 13 numbered experiments. The 57% sparse-poisoning boundary is in the paper. The DK weighting boundary is characterized. The γ magnitude is pilot-gated. Every claim states what it doesn't yet know.

The Conservation Law

Why this matters:

  • Every "self-improving AI" paper claims safety. Almost none prove it structurally. These six invariants compose — and each has a named failure mode if removed.
  • I1 (decision-form invariance) is what makes self-improvement approvable by a risk committee, not just demonstrable in a lab.

Three layers, not one

What Compounds

Why this matters:

  • RL systems learn from every outcome — including noise. RLHF systems learn from human preferences — including inconsistent ones. This system learns only when the math says it has enough evidence.
  • The 57% sparse-poisoning detection boundary is published. Most vendors don't know their boundary exists, let alone where it is.
Scoring Accuracy
  • 71.7% → 78.9% over 1,000 verified decisions
  • Zero-learning: 90.6% (four-action, no training data)
  • Centroids saturate near 200 decisions per class
  • Calibration tradeoff: learning improves accuracy but degrades ECE (0.053 static → 0.155 gated). No strategy is Pareto-dominant. Published, not hidden.
The Moat
  • Competitor trained on different firm's stream: never reaches parity
  • Gap: 19.6 ± 5.4 pp (SOC), 5.7 ± 1.1 pp (DataOps)
  • Closes only with ~half the incumbent's labeled verified stream
  • Non-transferable, not un-copyable

The compounding curve

Recovery dynamics

  • After a shock, accumulated geometry speeds re-calibration
  • Proved via four structural paths, confirmed in simulation
  • γ ≈ 1.2 calibrated; magnitude pilot-gated
  • Business reading: "should we rebuild after the campaign?" — no

Discovery scaling

  • Cross-attention between domain graphs: 111× above random (with normalization)
  • At six domains: 15 heads, ~3.75M pairwise scores, <2 seconds per sweep
  • The excess 0.11 over n² = cross-discovery cascade (confirmed by JM apparatus)

The Kernel Finding

Five kernels tested on bounded [0,1] factor vectors. 10 seeds x 10,000 alerts per seed. Mahalanobis and the learned kernel received training data (50/50 split); L2, cosine, and dot product did not.

KernelAccuracy +/- stdvs L2Sees training data?
Dot product60.900% +/- 0.704%-36.988 ppNo
Cosine96.448% +/- 0.366%-1.440 ppNo
Learned metric97.694% +/- 0.163%-0.194 ppYes (50%)
L297.888% +/- 0.152%baselineNo
Mahalanobis (OAS)97.898% +/- 0.161%+0.010 ppYes (50%)
  • Mahalanobis nominally wins by 0.010 pp — immaterial relative to seed variation (+/-0.15%). L2 and Mahalanobis are statistically tied.
  • L2 matches trained full-covariance distance without seeing any data. It is the correct default for bounded features.
  • The learned kernel failed to improve on L2 despite receiving training data — the feature space is too simple for learned structure to help.
  • Dot product loses 36.99 pp — magnitude confounding on bounded [0,1] features. The largest single-variable effect in the experiment program.
  • Cosine recovers most of the gap (96.4%) — removes magnitude, but loses boundary sensitivity that L2 preserves.

The weighting boundary (DK)

  • Per-factor inverse-variance weighting (DiagonalKernel) is preprocessing-dependent
  • L2 retained as default — Mahalanobis ties it, confirming L2 is the robust default, not a limitation
  • σ remains diagnostic (trust trap), not a scoring weight
  • The separation (I2) is why this is a clean boundary: learning and enrichment are independent

Why this matters:

  • 5-kernel systematic comparison. L2 ties the best trained alternative and beats every untrained one. Not a cherry-picked pair — every reasonable kernel family tested head-to-head.
  • +36.99pp from changing one character in the scoring function. If you are scoring bounded features with dot product, you are losing 37 points of accuracy to a confounding effect most implementations don't test for.
  • The learned kernel had an explicit advantage (training data) and still could not beat L2. On bounded features, the geometry is simple enough that the correct kernel is known, not learned.

Judgment Memory

The four cognitive-architecture memory types — and which graph operation produces each:

Memory typeStoresAnswersGraph operation
Episodicwhat happened"did we see this before?"read
Semanticwhat is true"what do we know about X?"read
Proceduralhow to act"what should I do here?"route
Judgmenthow well decisions are made, and where they are noise"how reliably does action A work in situation S?"reshape
  • Read and route extend existing memory types with better structure
  • Reshape adds a memory type the others cannot produce
  • It is the one that compounds

The trust trap (signal-confidence inversion)

  • Factor analysts report highest confidence in: device_trust (mean 4.2/5)
  • That factor has the highest outcome-conditioned variance: σ = 0.28
  • Factor they rate routine (threat_intel) has the lowest: σ = 0.07
  • Structurally invisible to episodic, semantic, and procedural memory
  • Only judgment memory surfaces this — and it compounds

Why this matters:

  • CoALA (Sumers et al.) defines three memory types for cognitive architectures. Judgment memory is a fourth — and it is the only one that compounds. No read or route can derive it.
  • The trust trap is the killer app: the factor your team trusts most is the noisiest. No dashboard shows this. No episodic or semantic memory can compute it. Only outcome-conditioned variance can.

Limits and Open Questions

Known boundaries
  • Sparse targeted poisoning — conservation detects sustained and sudden degradation at 100%. Sparse adversarial injection boundary: 57% poisoned decisions. Published, not hidden.
  • DK weighting — diagonal kernel (per-factor weights) is preprocessing-dependent. L2 identity retained as default. Characterized as a boundary, not a limitation.
  • γ magnitude — re-convergence ratio γ > 1 is proved. Exact magnitude (γ ≈ 1.2 calibrated) is pilot-gated pending production validation.
  • Single-firm data — ~194 experiments, one firm's operational data. Cross-firm generalization inferred from moat experiments, not demonstrated in production.
Open questions
  • Ablation tables — ✅ RESOLVED. Systematic I1–I6 ablation: all 6 accounted for. 5 confirmed failures (I6 largest: −12.08pp). I4 boundary defined via 18-config parameter sweep: protective above 60% adversarial intensity (+8pp→+34pp), engine self-corrects below 50%.
  • Additional baselines — ✅ RESOLVED. EXP-C1b: 5-kernel comparison (dot, cosine, L2, Mahalanobis, learned metric). L2 ties Mahalanobis, beats all others.
  • Data provenance — ✅ RESOLVED. Reproduction manifest maps every experiment ID to its script → data → chart → figure chain. 79 experiments, 17 chart scripts, 6 harnesses documented. Chain: experiment script → JSON results → chart script → PNG/PDF → page.
  • Calibration — ✅ RESOLVED. ECE measured across 5 strategies × 5 seeds. Finding: accuracy–calibration tradeoff. STATIC best ECE (0.0532), GATE_DECAY best accuracy (84.4%, ECE 0.1554). No strategy Pareto-dominant. Learning improves accuracy but degrades calibration — a documented tradeoff, not a defect.
  • Formal proofs — I1–I6 hold by construction in the code. Formal proof objects (Coq/Lean) are a potential future step.

  • Cross-domain discovery — a fix in procurement improves security scoring. Automatically.
